name: PAS (Problem, Agitate, Solution)
summary: Name the problem, intensify it by showing consequences, then relieve it with the solution.
references: Direct-response copywriting formula; see Dan Kennedy, The Ultimate Sales Letter (1990)
title_style: Short, pointed titles, under 10 words, written to 'you'.

sequence.purpose: Agitate: the cost of the problem.

pitfalls: Agitating so hard it feels manipulative.
A solution that does not directly answer the agitated pain.
Skipping the problem and leading with the product.

example.topic: A fictional scheduling tool for distributed teams
outline: Your team misses meetings across time zones
Each missed call delays a decision by a day
Three missed calls a week, in a team of eight
One calendar that shows everyone's local hour
Meetings land when people are awake
Try it with your team for two weeks
